content: The Argdown reference treats relation nesting as recursive: a relation's target element (statement or argument, ref or def) can itself carry deeper-indented child relations; more-indented lines are children, equal-indent lines are siblings.
rationale:
Agent probed reference via export_json on `[A]
  + [B]
    - [C]
  + [D]` and `<Arg>
  + [B]
  - <Arg2>
    +> [E]`, then concluded: 'the structure is recursive: element → child relations → each relation has an operator + direction + a target element → that target has its own child relations.'

content: In Argdown the outbound operator `+>` produces a parent→target edge (e.g. under `- <Arg2>`, a child `+> [E]` yields the edge Arg2 → E), distinct from inbound `+` which yields target → parent.
rationale: Agent verified via export_json that `+>` under an argument produced relation `from: Arg2, to: E`, and summarized: '`+>` confirmed outbound (parent→child).'

content: The existing `skip_trivia` greedily consumes all whitespace including the next line's leading indent, but relations need that indent as a depth signal — forcing a rework to a line-structured skip that stops at the leading indent of a content-bearing line.
rationale: Design doc states: 'Today skip_trivia greedily eats all whitespace including the next line's leading indent. Relations need that indent, so skip_trivia is reworked to be line-structured... but stops at the leading indent of a content-bearing line, leaving it for the block parser to measure.'

content: Chose to make the relation AST additive — a new `Block::Relation` variant carrying raw `indent: usize` — leaving `Statement`/`Argument` structs untouched so no existing A1/A2a test literals break and tree-building is deferred to Layer B.
rationale: Agent noted flat-with-depth 'keeps the parser a pure line recognizer (consistent with A1) and avoids touching the Statement/Argument structs' and 'Statement/Argument are unchanged → no existing test literals break (only Block gains a variant).' (Note: high-level nested-vs-flat was operator-decided; this AST shaping was the agent's.)

content: Decided to collapse the `+` and `<+` operators to the same `(Support, Inbound)` value (and similarly `-`/`<-`, `_`/`<_`), treating them as semantically identical.
rationale: Design doc: '`+` and `<+` collapse to the same (Support, Inbound) — they're semantically identical (the reference produces identical edges).' Agent did not explicitly test `<+` in the transcript, basing it on a claim about the reference.

content: Chose a block-dispatch order of heading → relation → argument → statement, with operator parsing trying 2-char tokens before 1-char (`+>` before `+`), relying on `<Title>` arguments to fall through the `<+`/`<-`/`<_` relation matchers.
rationale: Design doc: 'block tries: heading, relation (operator tokens; <+/<-/<_ match <+/-/_, so a <Title> argument falls through), argument, statement. Operator parsing tries 2-char tokens before 1-char (+> before +).'

content: Decided to add a 'not a relation marker' check to the `at_content_line` guard in text.rs so a multi-line target's text stops at the next relation line, making `[A]\n  + [B]` parse as a reference followed by a child relation block rather than an error.
rationale: Design doc: 'One guard change: at_content_line (in text.rs) gains a not a relation marker check. This both stops a multi-line target's text from swallowing the next relation line, and makes [A]\n  + [B] parse as a reference followed by a child relation block (no error).'

content: Chose to reuse the A2a argument/statement parsers verbatim for relation targets, so ref/def/plain forms for both statements and arguments — plus the strict text-after-reference error — work in relation position without new parsing code.
rationale: Design doc: 'The target reuses the A2a argument/statement parsers verbatim — so + [B], + [B]: x, + plain, + <Arg>, + <Arg>: x all work, including the strict text-after-reference error.'

content: The `skip_trivia` rework is the single place in A2b with real regression risk; the existing A1/A2a test suite is the safety net guarding it.
rationale: Design doc Impact section: 'The skip_trivia rework is the one place with regression risk — the existing A1/A2a tests are the safety net.'

content: Interspersed relations are modeled as a PcsItem::Relation rather than document-level sibling blocks, so the PCS stays one contiguous block while relations remain flat siblings for Layer B to associate by indent.

content: PCS is represented as a flat Vec<PcsItem> recording form (numbered statement / inference+rules / relation) but not role; premise/conclusion assignment and inference→conclusion binding are deferred to the semantic layer (Layer B).

content: A leading PcsItem::Statement cannot derive the PCS block start from statement.span, because statement.span begins after the `(n)` marker — losing the marker's byte position. Each PcsItem::Statement was therefore given its own marker→content span.

content: winnow's take_until(0.., "--") does not stop at line endings, so a ruled-divider parser written that way can scan past the current line and grab a distant '--' divider; divider content must be explicitly line-bounded (take_till on ['\r','\n']).
rationale: Self-review caught this: 'ruled_divider could scan across line endings via take_until(0.., "--") and grab a distant divider — a real bug. Rewriting it to bound content to the current line.' Fixed by switching to preceded("--", take_till(...)) + verify_map strip_suffix.

content: For A4 inline markup, chose representation Approach A: keep the normalized text string with markup retained and add a flat Vec<Inline> of typed elements, each carrying a true source byte span; nesting falls out of span containment rather than recursion.
rationale: After the M2 brain-jam, the agent concluded 'the jam settles representation on A (B rejected, C dissolved)' and the design specified `inlines: Vec<Inline>` as 'a flat list in source order; nesting is expressed by span containment, not recursion.'

content: Rejected Approach B (strip delimiters so text is display-ready, offsets point into cleaned string) as broken, not merely suboptimal, because offsets into a cleaned string have no stable mapping back to source — defeating error messages, IDE tooling, diff highlighting, and refactoring that all need source positions.
rationale: Agent relayed the jam's verdict: 'B isn't suboptimal, it's broken (R1). Offsets into a cleaned string have no stable meaning without a back-map to source... B discards that. Decisive against B.'

content: Rejected Approach C (replace text String with a recursive Vec<Inline> node tree); its only real advantage (containment queries) was reframed as a spatial interval-index problem solvable lazily over a flat span list, not a reason to store a tree.
rationale: Agent: 'C's only real advantage (containment queries) is a spatial-index problem, not a reason to store a tree... if profiling ever demands more, build an interval index lazily as an external free function over &[Span] — never a cache field on the node.'

content: The agent's seed worry — that retaining raw markup in `text` is a 'false economy' forcing every consumer to re-strip — was reframed as a misframe: stripping `**` is normalization (like whitespace-trimming), not interpretation, so it can be a thin derived `clean_text` helper rather than baked into the AST.
rationale: Agent: 'My worry ("raw markup in text is a false economy") was a misframe: stripping ** is closer to whitespace-trimming than to semantic work. So the fix isn't to bake cleaned text into the node... it's to expose a thin clean_text() helper returning Cow<'_, str>.'

content: Decided the clean_text rendering helper should return Cow<'_, str> (borrow source when emphasis only wraps content, allocate only when content is rewritten like [text](url)) and be a free function rather than an AST field, keeping spans canonical.
rationale: Design spec: 'a small clean_text(text, &inlines) -> Cow<str> helper (borrows source when emphasis only wraps content; allocates when content is rewritten, e.g. links)... It's a free function, not an AST field — the spans stay canonical.'

content: The brain-jam surfaced error recovery for malformed inline markup as an orthogonal axis that none of the A/B/C storage strategies address, prompting a separate user decision.
rationale: Agent: 'Plus a genuinely orthogonal axis the jam surfaced (R2): error recovery. A/B/C are storage strategies; none address malformed markup.' This led directly to the AskUserQuestion on inline error policy.

content: After the user picked 'Strict (parse error)' for malformed inline, the agent flagged that strict-as-previewed would reject ordinary prose (cost is 5 * 3, email a@b, item #1) and paused to verify reference behavior and escaping before locking it in, rather than implementing the literal binary choice.
rationale: Agent: 'the strict choice as previewed has a sharp consequence — it would reject ordinary prose like cost is 5 * 3... That might be exactly what you want... but it usually pairs with an escape mechanism... Let me check what the reference actually does.'

content: Reference @argdown/core probe: errors on unclosed `**bold` ('Incomplete bold text range... use \ to escape any character') but tolerates `5 * 3`, `#1`, and `a@b` as literal — so the reference is strict on completion but context-gates recognition (a delimiter only opens markup when adjacent to non-whitespace) and supports `\` escaping.
rationale: export_json probe returned 'parse L1:93: Incomplete bold text range' for the unclosed **, while the same input's 5*3/#1/a@b did not error. Agent concluded: 'Strict on completion... Context-gated recognition... Escaping: \ makes any character literal.'

content: Settled the A4 error model as 'strict on completion, context-gated on recognition': an unambiguously opened element that fails to close (unclosed **, [text]( with no ), @[/@< with no closer) is a hard Err{message, offset}; characters that never form a recognized opener stay literal with no error.
rationale: Design spec error model: 'an unambiguously opened element that doesn't complete is a hard Err{message, offset}... Characters that never form a recognized opener stay literal (no error). This sits alongside the existing block-level strict fail-fast.'

content: Adopted a simplified-flanking emphasis rule (delimiter run opens only when followed by non-whitespace, closes only when preceded by non-whitespace) plus an extra word-boundary guard for _/__ to keep snake_case literal; full CommonMark flanking is explicitly not implemented.
rationale: Design spec: 'This simplified-flanking rule is the one fiddly part; full CommonMark flanking is not implemented' and 'For _/__, an added word-boundary guard (not intra-word) keeps snake_case literal.'

content: A4 ends the project's no-churn streak: enriching statement/argument bodies forces every existing Statement/Argument test literal to gain `inlines: vec![]`, unlike A1/A2b/A3 which added structure without churning existing literals.
rationale: Design spec: 'every existing Statement/Argument test literal gains inlines: vec![] — the no-churn streak ends here (inherent to enriching text bodies); Heading is untouched.'

content: Scoped A4 to recognize inline form only (bold, italic, link, statement-mention, argument-mention, tag) in statement text and argument descriptions; headings stay raw, mention/tag resolution stays Layer B, and {yaml} metadata stays A5.
rationale: Design spec scope: 'recognize inline elements within statement text and argument descriptions... Headings stay raw (out of scope). Mention/tag resolution... stays Layer B — A4 recognizes form only. {yaml} metadata stays A5.'

content: The agent flagged two design calls as genuinely uncertain and worth operator input: (a) including _/__ emphasis with the word-boundary guard vs deferring to keep A4 simpler, and (b) including the clean_text helper in A4 vs deferring it to Layer B.
rationale: Agent: 'Two calls I'd especially flag: (a) including _/__ emphasis (with the word-boundary guard) vs deferring it to keep A4 simpler, and (b) including the clean_text helper in A4 vs deferring it until Layer B.'

content: The agent's seed worry — that retaining raw markup in `text` is a 'false economy' forcing every consumer to re-strip — was reframed as a misframe: stripping `**` is normalization (like whitespace-trimming), not interpretation, so it can be a thin derived `clean_text` helper rather than baked into the AST.

content: Inline recognition is per source body line — elements do not cross line breaks, and a recognized opener with no closer on its line is a hard parse failure (InlineError → ErrMode::Cut).

content: Emphasis recognition tries bold before italic, requires the opener be followed by a non-space non-same-delimiter char, and for `_` adds a word-boundary guard (the char before the opener must not be alphanumeric) so prose like `snake_case` stays literal.
rationale: try_emphasis in plan: 'Bold is tried first', 'Opener must be followed by a non-space, non-same-delimiter char', 'For _, the char before the opener must not be alphanumeric (word guard).'

content: Mentions (`@[]`/`@<>`) return Option (a lone `@` or unclosed mention is just literal, never an error), in deliberate contrast to emphasis, links, and parenthesized tags which return Result and error on an unclosed recognized opener.
rationale: Plan Task 4 note: 'mentions never error — a lone @ or @[ with no closer is just literal, so this recognizer returns Option, not Result.'

content: Links containing `//` in their URL are recognized correctly because `recognize` runs the link arm before the trailing `//`-comment stop is checked, so the comment stop only applies at the top level when no element opens.
rationale: Plan Task 3 header: 'including URLs containing // (the link is recognized before any comment stop because recognize runs first).'

content: A leading `_` emphasis line like `_i_ and __b__` is swallowed by the block-level `relation` dispatch arm before `statement` is tried, because `relation_operator` matches `_` as an Undercut operator and `inline_ws` allows zero following spaces — so the italic statement parses as an undercut relation instead.
rationale: Task 2 implementer reported BLOCKED: 'relation_operator in relation.rs matches a leading `_` as an Undercut operator without requiring following whitespace ... So `_i_ and __b__` parses as a Relation whose target is the statement `i_ and __b__`'.

content: The reference @argdown/core parser distinguishes emphasis from relations purely by a trailing space after the operator: `_this whole thing is italic_` parses as a statement, while `_ [Q]` (underscore + space) parses as an incoming undercut relation.
rationale: Controller verified the correct behavior against the live argdown MCP before deciding the fix: `mcp__argdown__parse` on `_this whole thing is italic_` returned 1 statement, and `_ [Q]` returned the 'paragraphs may not start with an incoming undercut relation (<_)' error.

content: Fixed the emphasis/relation ambiguity by requiring `take_while(1.., [' ','\t'])` after the relation operator, placed BEFORE the `cut_err(relation_target)` so a no-space line backtracks to `statement` rather than hard-erroring. This was an out-of-Task-2-scope change to relation.rs accepted as a prerequisite.
rationale: Controller chose option 1 (minimal relation.rs change) over revising the test, after confirming every existing A2b/PCS test already puts a space after the operator so nothing regresses; the take_while sits outside cut_err specifically to allow backtracking.

content: The trailing-space relation fix silently changed `_>word` (and similar glued operator+target with no space) from a permissively-parsed relation into a hard Cut parse error, because the no-space line backtracks to statement and the unclosed `_` emphasis opener then errors.
rationale: Task 2 code-quality review flagged this as Important: 'Before this commit ... `_>word` was a valid outbound-undercut relation. After this commit ... none found → Err(InlineError) → ErrMode::Cut.'

content: Inline elements are represented as a flat `Vec<Inline>` of typed ABSOLUTE source-byte spans, with nesting expressed via span containment (parent pushed before recursing into its content) rather than a tree; `text`/`description` strings stay unchanged.
rationale: Repeatedly enforced across dispatches and confirmed in final review: 'the representation (flat source-span inlines) was deliberately chosen and must be preserved'; final review verified `[T]: **b**` → bold span {5,10} with nesting by containment.

content: The inline scanner is a plain recursive Rust module (not winnow), `scan_line → scan_run → recognize → try_*`, byte-indexing `line.as_bytes()` with UTF-8-aware advancement via `char_len`. UTF-8 panic safety became the recurring focus of every recognizer review.
rationale: Quality reviews repeatedly traced byte-index sites for panic risk; final review: 'every slice site ... is bounded by an ASCII delimiter match ... ASCII bytes can only occur at char boundaries, so all slice endpoints land on boundaries.'

content: The strict-completion error model is encoded in the recognizer signatures: emphasis/link/tag return `Result` (unclosed markup → InlineError → hard ErrMode::Cut), while mentions return `Option` (a lone `@` or unclosed `@[`/`@<` is just literal, never an error).
rationale: Per-task instructions and final review confirm: 'the Result/Option split (mentions never error, emphasis/link/tag can) encoded honestly in the signatures'; try_mention's recognize arm uses `if let Some` (no `?`) while try_tag uses `?`.

content: Decision records and observations.jsonl must be committed separately from code: when an implementer bundled the four A4 decision MADRs + observations.jsonl into the Task 2 feat commit, the controller did `git reset --soft` and split them into a separate `docs:` commit, then instructed every subsequent implementer to stage ONLY `crates/`.
rationale: Controller: 'the implementer bundled the A4 decision records + observations.jsonl into the code commit. Same cleanliness issue as before — I'll split them out before reviewing,' then split into f88bb91 (code) + 28d7606 (docs).

content: The SendMessage tool to continue a prior subagent with its context intact is not available in this harness, so the controller could not hand fix-ups back to the original implementer and instead dispatched fresh subagents (e.g. to finish Task 2 from the staged working tree).
rationale: Controller ran ToolSearch for SendMessage, got 'No matching deferred tools found', and noted 'SendMessage isn't available in this harness ... I'll dispatch a fresh implementer to finish Task 2'.

content: Although the plan deferred `cargo fmt` to Task 8, the controller chose to run fmt and amend it into the Task 3 commit after a review flagged unformatted code, and added an explicit 'run cargo fmt --all --check before committing' instruction to all subsequent implementer prompts to prevent recurrence.
rationale: Controller: 'the plan defers fmt to Task 8, leaving intermediate commits unformatted is poor practice and the fix is trivial. I'll format now and amend it into Task 3's commit ... so it doesn't recur.'

content: Adding tag recognition correctly changed a pre-existing test expectation: `#nospace` still parses as a Block::Statement (heading requires a space after `#`) but now additionally carries a `Tag { tag: "nospace" }` inline spanning bytes 0..8. The implementer updated the expectation rather than weakening the tag implementation.
rationale: Implementer flagged the change and review confirmed 'correct and not a hack ... the statement/heading distinction is unchanged ... the test now asserts more behavior, not less.'

content: Word-guard and tag recognition are ASCII-only (`is_alnum`/`is_tag_char`): a non-ASCII letter adjacent to `_` does not trigger the emphasis word guard, and a tag run stops at the first non-ASCII byte. This is a recognition approximation accepted for A4 scope, not a panic risk.
rationale: Final review minor issue: 'is_tag_char/is_alnum are ASCII-only, so word-guard and tag recognition are an ASCII approximation ... Acceptable for A4 and consistent with the simplified-flanking decision; worth one line of doc.'

content: For the recognizer-addition tasks (links/mentions/tags), the controller collapsed the two-stage spec-then-quality review into a single combined spec+quality review with a UTF-8-safety focus, relying on the Task 8 whole-implementation review as backstop, reasoning these tasks are small and structurally identical to the already-reviewed emphasis recognizer.
rationale: Controller: 'These recognizer-addition tasks (3–5) are small, well-specified, and structurally identical to the already-reviewed emphasis recognizer, so I'll run one combined spec+quality review each ... and rely on the Task 8 whole-implementation review as the backstop.'

content: Model selection was tiered to task complexity: mechanical recognizer/test tasks (1, 3–7) and per-task reviews were dispatched to sonnet, while the Task 2 integration crux and the final whole-implementation review were left on the more capable default (opus) model.
rationale: Controller dispatched Tasks 1/3/4/5/6/7 with `model: sonnet` but Task 2 ('the integration crux ... I'll give this one the more capable model') and the final review with no model override (default opus).

content: A4 chose to represent inline elements (bold, italic, links, @[]/@<> mentions, #tag) as a flat Vec<Inline> of typed absolute source-byte spans overlaid on the body, with nesting expressed by span containment.
rationale: ADR TRADEOFFS entry: 'A4 emits inline elements ... as a flat Vec<Inline> of typed absolute source-byte spans overlaid on the body, nesting expressed by span containment — over the reference's cleaned-text-with-ranges or a recursive inline node tree.'

content: A4 is the first increment to add a field (inlines) to existing Statement/Argument nodes, ending the prior streak of purely additive Block-variant growth with zero churn through A3.
rationale: ADR: 'Growth was additive with zero churn through A3 ...; A4 is the first increment to add a field (inlines) to Statement/Argument, ending that streak — inline intrinsically enriches the text body, so the inlines: vec![] literal churn was the accepted price.'

content: The A4 representation brain-jam rejected the reference's cleaned-text-with-ranges model as broken because offsets into a derived string lose the source mapping that diagnostics/tooling need.
rationale: ADR: 'A4's representation jam also rejected the reference's cleaned-text model as broken — offsets into a derived string lose the source mapping that diagnostics/tooling need.'

content: The node-tree option for inline was dissolved on the grounds that containment queries are a spatial/interval-index concern, not a reason to store a tree; cleaning and any interval index are deferred to a real consumer.
rationale: ADR: 'dissolved the node-tree option: containment queries are a spatial/interval-index concern, not a reason to store a tree. So inline stays flat source spans; cleaning and any interval index are deferred to a real consumer.'

content: A4 surfaced and fixed a latent A2b bug: a relation operator now requires a trailing space, so `_italic_` parses as a statement rather than an undercut relation, and the glued `+[B]` form becomes a statement — aligning with the reference.
rationale: ADR: 'A4 also surfaced and fixed a latent A2b bug: a relation operator now requires a trailing space, so _italic_ is a statement, not an undercut relation (reference-aligned; the glued +[B] form becomes a statement).' Also confirmed in final summary as the `_i_` block-dispatch bug escalated by the implementer and fixed in relation.rs.

content: A4 keeps the project's strict fail-fast error model uniform (unclosed **, [text](, #( all error) but context-gates inline recognition via simplified flanking plus a `_` word-boundary guard and `\` escaping, so ordinary prose (5 * 3, snake_case, a@b, [1]) stays literal and never errors.
rationale: ADR error-model entry: 'A4 keeps the strictness uniform ... but context-gates recognition (simplified flanking + a _ word-boundary guard) plus \ escaping, so ordinary prose ... stays literal and never errors.'

content: A4 was scoped as 'full inline' — the entire inline vocabulary (bold, italic, links, statement-mentions @[T], argument-mentions @<T>, tags #tag) in one increment — rather than the smaller emphasis-only A4a slice.
rationale: Prepare CLI output of new MADR: 'How should we scope the A4 (inline) increment — Chose Full inline. The entire inline vocabulary in one increment ... Largest slice; mentions are inline cross-references (their resolution stays Layer B, but recognizing them is A4).'

content: A4's inline recognition runs inside the shared body readers (definition_body, plain_statement), so argument descriptions and PCS numbered statements get inlines for free.
rationale: ADR reuse entry: 'A4's inline recognition runs inside the shared body readers (definition_body, plain_statement), so argument descriptions and PCS numbered statements get inlines for free.'

content: The agent distilled a new lead philosophy principle from the A4 decisions: 'Every span is a source range' — positions index the original source, never a derived/cleaned string, an invariant treated as load-bearing for diagnostics and tooling.
rationale: New PHILOSOPHY bullet authored during sync: 'Every span is a source range. Positions index the original source, never a derived/cleaned string — that invariant is load-bearing for diagnostics and tooling and is the reason a cleaned-text inline representation was rejected.'

rationale: After probing `[Claim]: A statement. {certainty: 0.8, tags: [a, b]}` the agent observed: 'Metadata `{...}` is consumed (the text drops it) but `export_json` didn't surface a `data` field here.' The JSON result showed text 'A statement. ' with no metadata field.

content: A5 metadata surface spans multiple attachment sites — statements, arguments, headings/sections, inference lines — plus document frontmatter (`===`…`===`); the content is YAML (key/values, lists, nested maps, quoted strings) and the reference special-cases a `tags` key.
rationale: Agent summarized after two probes: 'metadata `{yaml}` attaches to multiple sites — statements, arguments, headings/sections, and inference lines — plus document frontmatter. The content is YAML... the reference parses it into structured data (and special-cases a `tags` key).'

content: Tag-promotion (the reference lifting a `tags:` key from metadata into the element's tag set) is deferred to semantic Layer B, consistent with A4 having deferred tag aggregation.
rationale: Agent stated after scope lock: 'Tag-promotion — the reference lifting a `tags:` key into the element's tag set — stays Layer B, consistent with A4 deferring tag aggregation.'

content: Recommended Approach A for metadata: brace-match the `{…}` block (depth- and quote-aware), capture only its inner-content source span, strip it from the element's text, and defer YAML parsing to Layer B — keeping the parser a pure recognizer with no new dependency.
rationale: Agent presented three approaches (A raw span stripped, B raw string+span, C parsed YAML via serde_yaml) and concluded 'My lean: A. It keeps the parser a pure recognizer, every span a source range, and adds no dependency — and stripping trailing metadata from `text` mirrors how we already drop trailing comments.'

content: Stripping metadata out of the text field may be inconsistent with A4's choice to keep inline markup inside text as an overlay — unless metadata is genuinely a different kind of thing (about the element) rather than prose markup (part of the element).
rationale: Agent flagged the tension: '"strip vs retain (A4 kept markup in text)"... genuinely cross-cut'; the M2 seed phrased it as 'the prior increment deliberately KEPT markup inside the text field as an overlay, but here I propose STRIPPING metadata out — is that an inconsistency, or is metadata genuinely a different kind of thing from prose markup?'

content: The 'pure recognizer, no parsing' framing for metadata is partly a fiction: safely locating the closing brace requires tracking depth and respecting quotes/brackets, i.e. partial YAML lexing is unavoidable even under Approach A.
rationale: Agent's M2 seed: 'to even find the closing brace safely I must track depth and respect quotes/brackets, i.e. I am already doing partial YAML lexing — so the "pure recognizer, no parsing" framing is partly a fiction.'

content: Deferring the YAML parse to Layer B risks a false economy: unlike inline emphasis whose meaning is the prose, a metadata block's entire value is its structured content, so deferring may relocate identical YAML work to N consumers.
rationale: Agent's M2 seed raised: 'a metadata block's entire value is its structured content, so deferring the parse may just relocate identical YAML work to N consumers — the same false-economy worry we hit with a clean-text helper in the prior increment, which we resolved by deferring.'

content: Chose metadata representation Option B (Metadata { raw: String, span: Span }, stripped from text) over span-only (A) and parse-YAML-now (C) for A5a.
rationale: After reading the M2 brain-jam the agent moved off its initial lean toward A and concluded 'B beats A (span-only forces re-reading source and distributes the parse) and beats C (parses + adds a dependency in the recognizer, crossing the line — and prematurely, with no consumer)'; user then confirmed B via AskUserQuestion.

content: The A4 'defer cleaning' precedent does not transfer to metadata: prose markup is interpreted differently per consumer (deferral right), but a YAML parse is deterministic/universal, so deferring a bare span distributes identical parsing liability to N consumers.
rationale: Agent synthesis: 'deferring to N consumers isn't "deferring work," it's "distributing identical liability" — N copies of the parse, N malformed-metadata error paths, N version-divergence points.'

content: Metadata is stripped from the element's text field (text becomes clean), unlike A4 which intentionally kept inline markup inside text as an overlay; the strip-vs-retain asymmetry is treated as intentional.
rationale: Agent reasoned metadata is 'typed data about the element' while markup is 'rendering intent', resolving the strip-vs-retain inconsistency that nagged in the seed thoughts: 'strip it from text ... but ... keep the raw inner string accessible'.

content: The parser's 'pure recognizer, no parsing' self-description is partly fiction: depth- and quote-aware brace matching to find the closing } is itself lexing/a semantic judgment about where the block ends.
rationale: Agent conceded in the jam: 'Depth-tracking with quote-awareness is lexing, full stop. The "pure recognizer" claim was cover for the fact that I'd already decided the block boundary mattered.' — but concluded this argues for capturing the raw string, not for parsing now.

content: Multi-line {…} metadata blocks are supported by the reference parser: statement text strips to before the {, and the block body extends across newlines to the matching } (verified to span lines 1–4).

Inference-line metadata cleanly separates from rule names in the reference: '-- Modus Ponens {uses: [1,2]} --' yields inferenceRules ['Modus Ponens'], which fixes the A3 limitation where {…} polluted the captured rule name.
rationale: export_json probe returned 'inferenceRules': ['Modus Ponens']; agent: 'inference metadata is cleanly separated ... fixing A3's known limitation.'

content: '{' is effectively a reserved character: the reference treats the first unescaped { as the start of metadata, and any text after the closing } on an element is a hard error — metadata must be the last thing on the element, mirroring the text-after-reference rule.
rationale: Probe '[Set]: the set {a, b} is large and {final: true}' errored ('Expecting token of type EOF but found is large and'); text captured as 'the set '. Agent: 'the first unescaped { as the start of metadata ... text after the closing } is a hard error.'

content: A5 split into A5a (element {yaml} metadata at statement/argument/heading/inference sites) and A5b (document frontmatter via === fences), each its own spec→plan→build.
rationale: Agent flagged that the blast-radius decomposition flag fired and full A5 was 'the largest increment yet' (multi-line blocks, {-always-metadata + strict text-after, A4-escape interaction, 4 sites + distinct frontmatter fence); presented split as recommended; user selected 'Split: A5a then A5b'.

content: Relations carry no metadata field; metadata on a relation attaches to its target statement/argument via the reused statement/argument parsers.
rationale: Spec decision 5: '+ [B] {k: v} attaches the metadata to the target statement/argument (recognized via the reused parsers), so the relation itself carries none.'

content: A { inside a recognized A4 inline element (link URL/display text, mention) must not open metadata; the metadata opener is the first unescaped TOP-LEVEL {, requiring metadata detection to interleave with inline recognition.
rationale: Agent self-review of the spec: 'one ambiguity to fix — the interaction between A4 inline elements and metadata { detection. A { inside a link URL or mention shouldn't be a metadata opener.' — then added an explicit spec clause.

content: Deferred to Layer B: YAML parsing, the serde_yaml dependency, a single canonical parse_metadata(&str) utility with a crate-owned MetadataError enum (not leaking serde_yaml::Error), and tags-key promotion.
rationale: Spec decision 6 and jam synthesis: keep the recognizer dependency-free, centralize the parse in 'a single future Layer-B utility ... with a crate-owned error enum'; the jam's emergent point was that the error type is the one concentrated coupling worth owning.

content: A4's escape concept is reused at the body-reader level so that \{ is a literal brace and never opens a metadata block.
rationale: Spec decisions 2 and error model: 'A \{ is literal and never opens a block' and 'reuses A4's escape concept at the body-reader level'; testing table includes '[S]: a \{ literal brace → no metadata'.

content: The A4 'defer cleaning' precedent does not transfer to metadata: prose markup is interpreted differently by each consumer (so deferral is right), but a YAML parse is deterministic and universal, so deferring a bare span distributes identical parsing liability to N consumers rather than deferring work.
rationale: Agent synthesis from the jam: 'deferring to N consumers isn't "deferring work," it's "distributing identical liability" — N copies of the parse, N malformed-metadata error paths, N version-divergence points.'

content: Metadata is stripped from the element's text field (text becomes clean), unlike A4 which intentionally kept inline markup inside text as an overlay; the strip-vs-retain asymmetry with A4 is treated as intentional because metadata is typed data about the element, not prose rendering intent.
rationale: Agent resolved the strip-vs-retain inconsistency that nagged in its seed thoughts — 'strip it from text ... but keep the raw inner string accessible' — by distinguishing metadata (typed data) from markup (rendering intent).

content: The parser's 'pure recognizer, no parsing' self-description is partly fiction: depth- and quote-aware brace matching to locate the closing } is itself lexing / a semantic judgment about where the block ends.
rationale: Agent conceded the jam point — 'Depth-tracking with quote-awareness is lexing, full stop. The "pure recognizer" claim was cover for the fact that I'd already decided the block boundary mattered' — but concluded this argues for capturing the raw string, not for parsing now.

content: Multi-line {…} metadata blocks are supported by the reference parser: statement text strips to before the {, and the block body extends across newlines to the matching } (verified spanning lines 1–4).

Inference-line metadata cleanly separates from rule names in the reference: '-- Modus Ponens {uses: [1,2]} --' yields inferenceRules ['Modus Ponens'], which fixes the A3 limitation where the {…} polluted the captured rule name.
rationale: export_json probe returned 'inferenceRules': ['Modus Ponens']; agent noted A5a's inference handling 'fixes A3's known limitation.'

content: '{' is effectively a reserved character: the reference treats the first unescaped { as the start of metadata, and any text after the closing } on an element is a hard error — metadata must be the last thing on the element, mirroring the text-after-reference rule.
rationale: Probe '[Set]: the set {a, b} is large and {final: true}' errored ('Expecting token of type --> EOF <-- but found is large and'), text captured as 'the set '; agent: 'the first unescaped { as the start of metadata ... text after the closing } is a hard error.'

content: A5 was split into A5a (element {yaml} metadata at statement/argument/heading/inference sites) and A5b (document frontmatter via === fences), each getting its own spec→plan→build cycle.

Reconstructing a multi-line metadata block by re-joining continuation lines with hardcoded '
' silently corrupts spans on CRLF source: till_line_ending strips the original '
' (2 bytes) so the rebuilt block_src is 1 byte short per line break, drifting Metadata.span and writing '
' into raw where the source had '
'.
rationale:
Task 4 reviewer found: 'join_from re-joins continuation lines with 
 (1 byte), but till_line_ending strips the original 
 (2 bytes)... Metadata.span no longer indexes the original source, and raw reports 
 where the source had 
.' Verified against existing crlf_within_statement contract.

content: The CRLF span-drift fix captured the verbatim contiguous body source via winnow's .with_taken() and sliced the metadata block from real source bytes, deleting join_from entirely — making span/raw correct by construction for LF and CRLF, single- and multi-line.
rationale: Fix agent: 'I used the preferred approach: capture the verbatim contiguous body source via winnow's .with_taken() rather than reconstructing it... line endings are preserved verbatim and every offset is an exact absolute range. Deleted join_from entirely.'

content: brace_delta and capture_metadata initially diverged on escape handling: brace_delta treated '\' as a top-level escape outside quotes while capture_metadata only escapes inside double-quotes, breaking the documented 'mirrors capture_metadata' contract; they were later aligned so neither escapes '\' outside quotes.
rationale: Task 4 reviewer flagged 'brace_delta treats \ as a top-level escape (i += 2) while capture_metadata does not... the two functions are documented as mirroring each other and that claim is false.' Fix agent later removed the top-level escape arm from brace_delta.

content: winnow's .with_span() records the start position BEFORE the parser runs, so wrapping preceded(take_while(ws), till_line_ending) in with_span yields a span.start pointing at the leading whitespace, not the text — drifting the heading metadata span by the number of spaces between '#' and the title.
rationale: Task 5 reviewer: 'with_span() calls input.current_token_start() before the parser runs... text_span.start points one-or-more bytes earlier. For "# Title {k: v}" computed span.start = 7, actual = 8.' Fix was to consume whitespace as its own step first.

content: The strict 'text after closing } is a hard error' rule was enforced on statement/argument bodies but silently missing on headings (and later inference lines), so '# Title {k: v} garbage' parsed successfully and dropped 'garbage' until the gap was closed.
rationale: Task 5 reviewer: 'the heading parser silently ignores any text after the }... "# Title {k: v} garbage" succeeds with text = "Title"... heading does not have the tail-trivia check.' Same gap later flagged for inference lines in Task 6 review.

content: After the heading span-drift bug, the controller treated absolute-span offset errors as a recurring bug class and proactively instructed the Task 6 reviewer to numerically verify the inference metadata span for an element not at offset 0.
rationale: Controller dispatched Task 6 review with 'attention to the absolute span offset (given the analogous heading bug)' and the review prompt 'CRITICAL CHECK — metadata span offset... a sibling task had this exact bug... WRITE this assertion and run it.'

content: winnow's take(n) on a LocatingSlice<&str> input advances n CHARACTERS, not n bytes; using it with a byte-length (consumed = span.end - span.start) over-consumes whenever the metadata block contains a multibyte char, causing the reference branch to fail and silently backtrack to plain_statement — misclassifying e.g. '[Cafe] {nóte: x}' as a plain statement.
rationale: Task 7 reviewer: 'Input = LocatingSlice<&str>, whose token is char, so take(n) advances n characters... consumed (bytes) > char count, so take over-consumes... silently backtracks to plain_statement.' Fix replaced take(consumed) with literal(&line[..consumed]).

content: brace_delta and capture_metadata initially diverged on escape handling: brace_delta treated '\' as a top-level escape outside quotes (i += 2) while capture_metadata only escapes inside double-quotes, breaking the documented 'mirrors capture_metadata' contract; they were later aligned so neither escapes '\' outside quotes.
rationale: Task 4 reviewer (minor): 'brace_delta treats \ as a top-level escape while capture_metadata does not... the two functions are documented as mirroring each other and that claim is false.' Fix agent removed the top-level escape arm from brace_delta.

content: winnow's .with_span() snapshots the start position BEFORE the parser runs, so wrapping preceded(take_while(ws), till_line_ending) in with_span yields a span.start pointing at the leading whitespace rather than the text — drifting the heading metadata span by the number of spaces between '#' and the title. Fix: consume the whitespace as its own parse step first.
rationale: Task 5 reviewer (critical): 'with_span() calls input.current_token_start() before the parser runs... text_span.start points one-or-more bytes earlier. For "# Title {k: v}" computed span.start = 7, actual = 8.' The existing test did not assert metadata.span so it passed silently.

content: The strict 'text after closing } is a hard error' rule was enforced on statement/argument bodies but silently missing on headings (and later inference lines), so '# Title {k: v} garbage' parsed successfully and dropped 'garbage' until the gap was closed.
rationale: Task 5 reviewer: 'the heading parser silently ignores any text after the }... "# Title {k: v} garbage" succeeds with text = "Title"... heading does not have the tail-trivia check.' The same gap was independently flagged for inference lines in the Task 6 review.

content: After the heading span-drift bug, the controller treated absolute-span offset errors as a recurring bug class and proactively instructed the Task 6 reviewer to numerically verify the inference metadata span for an element not at offset 0 (writing and running an explicit assertion).
rationale: Controller dispatched Task 6 review 'with attention to the absolute span offset (given the analogous heading bug)' and the review prompt: 'CRITICAL CHECK — metadata span offset... a sibling task had this exact bug... WRITE this assertion and run it.'

content: The inference ruled_divider span base is content_span.start + 2: with_span on preceded("--", take_till(...)) starts at the first '-' of the opening '--', so the actual content begins 2 bytes later; the reviewer numerically confirmed the +2 yields exact spans (src[22..35] == "{uses: [1,2]}").
rationale: Task 6 reviewer: 'content_span.start = 6 (the first - of --)... content starts 2 bytes later, so base = content_span.start + 2 = 8... span.start = 22, span.end = 35. src[22..35] == "{uses: [1,2]}" — exact.'

content: winnow's take(n) on a LocatingSlice<&str> input advances n CHARACTERS, not n bytes; using it with a byte-length (consumed = span.end - span.start) over-consumes whenever the metadata block contains a multibyte char, causing the reference branch to fail and silently backtrack to plain_statement — misclassifying e.g. '[Cafe] {nóte: x}' as a plain statement. Fix: literal(&line[..consumed]) advances by the exact byte prefix.
rationale: Task 7 reviewer (critical): 'Input = LocatingSlice<&str>, whose token is char, so take(n) advances n characters... consumed (bytes) > char count, so take over-consumes... silently backtracks to plain_statement.' Definition/plain/heading/inference paths slice &str bytes directly and were unaffected.

content: When the Task 7 implementer subagent hit a transient server rate-limit before reporting, the controller inspected the working tree, found the work complete and green (95 passing tests, all Task 7 test names present) but uncommitted, verified clippy/fmt, and committed it directly as the controller rather than re-dispatching.
rationale: Controller: 'The rate-limited agent actually completed Task 7 in the working tree (uncommitted): 5 files modified, 95 tests pass... It got cut off before committing.' Then committed crates/ only.

content: Reference metadata was implemented as finish_reference_with_metadata = reference_metadata then the unchanged finish_reference, so [T] {k: v} captures the trailing block while [T] words still errors, [T] stays a bare reference, and [T] // comment still works; non-trivia before the { is rejected via a line[..open].trim() guard.
rationale: Task 7 reviewer: 'The reference guard is genuinely preserved (finish_reference_with_metadata = reference_metadata then the unchanged finish_reference)... reference_metadata correctly rejects non-trivia before the { (line[..open].trim() guard), so it can't swallow [T] foo {x}.'

content: The agent articulated a sharpened deferral principle: defer interpretation only when it varies by consumer (e.g. render-vs-strip markup); when a parse is deterministic and universal (YAML), capture the raw form once so a single downstream parse_metadata utility interprets it rather than distributing identical liability to N consumers.

content: The winnow expression repeat(0.., body_line).with_taken() type-inferred correctly with only the annotation `let (_, raw): ((), &str)` — no turbofish needed despite the controller anticipating a possible inference failure.
rationale: Task 2 implementer reported 'Code compiled as-is — no adjustments were needed... the type annotation inferred correctly without a turbofish,' contradicting the controller's pre-emptive note that it might need a turbofish.

content: repeat(0.., body_line) cannot infinite-loop because body_line guarantees ≥1 byte consumed per non-terminating iteration; the not(eof) guard is load-bearing, not redundant — without it an empty line at EOF would consume zero bytes and spin.
rationale: Task 2 code-quality reviewer analyzed termination: 'not(fence_line) guards the fence, not(eof) guards the end, and till_line_ending + opt(line_ending) guarantees at least one byte is consumed... so repeat cannot loop forever.'

content: The expected fence_line dead-code warning did not appear after Task 3; the implementer hypothesized Rust suppresses it in test mode or the pub(crate) visibility keeps it quiet.
rationale: Task 3 implementer noted: 'The fence_line dead-code warning is absent from the test run output — Rust appears to suppress it in test mode, or the pub(crate) visibility keeps it quiet.'

content: The second skip_trivia after opt(frontmatter) in document() is necessary, not redundant: frontmatter's trailing-break peek deliberately does NOT consume the blank line after the close fence, so something downstream must consume it before block parsing.
rationale: Task 3 code-quality reviewer traced the control flow: 'second skip_trivia consumes the blank separator line that frontmatter deliberately peeks but does not consume (required by D2)... Each of the three lines has a distinct, non-redundant purpose.'

content: Enforcing D2 (fences valid only at document start) was implemented with two cooperating mechanisms rather than one: not(fence_line) added to the shared at_content_line gate so continuation readers stop at a fence, plus a misplaced_fence cut-branch placed first in block() to hard-error at a block boundary.
rationale: Task 4 controller prompt and the spec reviewer both describe the paired design: '(a) continuation readers must STOP at a fence line... (b) the block dispatcher block() must reject a fence line at a block boundary with a hard Cut error.'

content: misplaced_fence must be the FIRST alternative in block()'s alt — otherwise the statement/continuation parsers would absorb a bare === line as prose text before the fence guard runs.
rationale: Task 4 code-quality reviewer: 'Placing misplaced_fence first in the alt is the only correct position — any statement or continuation parser might otherwise swallow the === as prose.'

content: Emitting a bare ErrMode::Cut(ContextError::new()) without a StrContext label matches the existing codebase norm; the only labeled cut errors wrap cut_err on a combinator in finish_reference, a structurally different call site.
rationale: Task 4 code-quality reviewer verified against siblings: 'text.rs lines 217, 223, 281 and pcs.rs lines 113, 126 all use bare ErrMode::Cut(ContextError::new()) with no StrContext::Label... No label is the right call here.'

content: Across Tasks 2, 3, and 4 the implementer subagents repeatedly produced rustfmt-noncompliant code (over-length assert_eq!, one-line struct literal, out-of-order crate:: imports) that only the code-quality review caught, since the implementers did not run cargo fmt --check.
rationale: Each task's code-quality review flagged a fmt violation as its required fix: Task 2 'cargo fmt --check fails on one line', Task 3 'rustfmt wants the one-liner expanded', Task 4 'use crate::frontmatter::fence_line must come after... alphabetical'.

content: The additive Document.frontmatter field required no change in argdown-mcp because that crate only Debug-prints Document — confirming the blast radius of the new field was confined to argdown-core and argdown-parser.
rationale: Final reviewer: 'argdown-mcp has no tests of its own (it only Debug-prints Document, so the additive field needs no change there — consistent with the plan's blast-radius note).'

content: The frontmatter raw body is captured via with_taken (verbatim source slice, CRLF preserved, never re-joined) and its span comes from the LocatingSlice so it stays absolute even after leading blank lines — applying lessons from A5a's two CRLF/offset span-drift bugs up front.
rationale: Final reviewer verified by reading code and throwaway tests: 'raw is the with_taken slice of the body... the span is captured from the locating slice so it indexes the original source even after leading blank lines,' tying it to A5a's prior span bugs.

content: A5b reused A5a's Metadata {raw, span} type verbatim for Document.frontmatter rather than inventing a new representation, which meant A5b needed no M2 brain-jam — its open questions were narrow strict/lenient policy knobs settled directly with the operator via AskUserQuestion.
rationale: During ADR synthesis the agent characterized A5b as 'the payoff of that framing... no new representation question, and so (unlike A3/A4/A5a) no new jam,' contrasting it with the representation jams of earlier increments.

rationale: Agent stated `--locked` "means we must commit the updated Cargo.lock" and in the design: "adding Criterion changes the lock, and --locked fails if it's stale."

content: Keep Criterion's `html_reports` feature off (default features only) so the plotters dependency stays out of the build, minimizing the CI bench-compile cost; the regression guard is the terminal % change, not SVG plots.
rationale: Design: "html_reports is deliberately off (the regression guard is terminal % change, not the SVG plots) — and since CI compiles benches (--all-targets), leaving plotters out keeps that cost down."

content: Centralize the criterion version in the root `[workspace.dependencies]` and pull it into the crate via `{ workspace = true }`, mirroring how `winnow` is already declared.
rationale: Design: "Version centralized the way winnow is (one canonical place)" with root workspace.dependencies and the crate's dev-dependencies referencing `{ workspace = true }`.

content: Benchmark only the public `parse()` entry point and not private sub-recognizers, so the bench suite stays stable across parser refactors.
rationale: Non-goals: "no benchmarking of private sub-recognizers (public parse() only, so it stays stable across refactors)."

content: Generate sized benchmark inputs from a corpus-as-code generator that repeats a representative 'unit' (corpus(1)/corpus(50)/corpus(500)) rather than committing static blob files, keeping sizes reproducible and version-controlled.
rationale: Design: "a generator emits one representative 'unit' ... and repeats it, so sizes are reproducible and version-controlled, not committed blobs."

content: A malformed corpus string would make parse() fail-fast, causing the benchmark to time the error path rather than parsing; an untimed `assert!(parse(src).is_ok())` before each timed run guards against silently meaningless numbers.
rationale: Design: "if a corpus string were malformed, parse() would fail-fast early and we'd be benchmarking the error path, not parsing. The assert ... makes an invalid corpus panic loudly instead of silently producing meaningless numbers."

content: With `harness = false` the bench is excluded from cargo test's #[test] discovery, so the in-bench corpus-validity assert is effectively the only check of corpus correctness.
rationale: Design: "Approach A keeps the corpus in the bench binary, which harness = false excludes from cargo test's #[test] discovery — so this in-bench assert is the corpus correctness check."

content: Task 1 implementer dropped `BenchmarkId` from the criterion import even though the plan listed it, because nothing in the `features` group used it yet and an unused import fails `clippy -D warnings`.
rationale: Implementer report: 'the plan's corpus import included BenchmarkId which is not used in the features group — it would be used by the scaling group (Task 2). Removed it before the clippy gate to keep -D warnings clean.' Controller confirmed Task 2 would re-add it.

content: `cargo bench -p argdown-parser -- --save-baseline main` fails with 'Unrecognized option: save-baseline' because bare `cargo bench` also runs the crate's default libtest harness, which rejects Criterion-only flags; the baseline workflow must target `--bench parse`.
rationale: Final verification run produced `error: Unrecognized option: 'save-baseline'`; agent reasoned 'cargo bench -p argdown-parser runs two bench targets — the lib's default #[test] harness and our Criterion parse bench... The fix is to target the bench explicitly with --bench parse.' Verified working with --bench parse.

content: Criterion 0.5's default features include `plotters` and `rayon`, so disabling `html_reports` does NOT keep them out of the build — the plotting/parallel stack still compiled on every CI `--all-targets` run, contradicting the 'no plotters' rationale in the docs.
rationale: Final reviewer verified libplotters_backend*.rlib and criterion_plot*.rlib were actually compiled into target/debug/deps, citing criterion-0.5.1's default feature set ['rayon','plotters','cargo_bench_support']. Agent: 'the shipped code under-delivers on the design's explicit lean compile goal, and the comment is false.'

content: Rather than soften the docs to match the accidental under-delivery, the agent fixed the dependency to actually realize intent: `default-features = false, features = ["cargo_bench_support"]`, dropping plotters+rayon while keeping `cargo bench` working.
rationale: Agent: 'don't soften the docs to match an accidental under-delivery — make the code actually do what it says.' Verified post-change: `cargo tree -i plotters`/`-i rayon` matched nothing and `cargo bench` still ran end-to-end.

content: The stray untracked `rust_out` was recognized as a 473K Mach-O executable — rustc's default output name when a .rs file is compiled directly without -o, likely left by a reviewer subagent invoking rustc on the bench file.
rationale: Agent inspected: 'never git-tracked, created today — that's rustc's default output name when a .rs file is compiled directly without -o. It's a stray build artifact... not part of this change and not something I created, so I'm not deleting it on my own.' Surfaced to operator rather than silently removing.

content: Parser throughput holds steady at ~51 MiB/s across small (1 unit), medium (50), and large (500) corpus sizes, confirming near-linear parse scaling with no hidden quadratic blowup.
rationale: Task 2 scaling results: scaling/small 5.66µs, medium 249µs, large 2.51ms, all ~51 MiB/s. Controller: 'the numbers are a nice sanity signal: ~51 MiB/s throughput holds steady across small→large, confirming near-linear parse scaling.'

content: The top-level Argument-definition recognizer (`<Title>: description`) is never benchmarked — the corpus exercises every Block variant except argument definitions, so a regression there would go unmeasured (a coverage gap, though consistent with the approved spec).
rationale: Final reviewer: 'Of the 5 Block variants... the corpus exercises all except a top-level Argument definition. <Counter {i}> is a relation target and @<Arg {i}> is an inline mention; neither hits the argument() definition recognizer (crates/argdown-parser/src/argument.rs:16).' Flagged as optional follow-up, not drift.

content: The recurring `Permission denied (os error 13)` on `~/.cargo/registry/.../regex-1.7.0/Cargo.toml` during clippy/build is a pre-existing global cargo-cache auto-clean quirk, not a defect in the change — clippy still exits 0.
rationale: Agent re-ran clippy with sandbox disabled and saw `clippy exit: 0` despite the permission line: 'cargo trying to remove a read-only file in the global ~/.cargo/registry cache — a pre-existing environment quirk in the shared registry, nothing to do with this code.'

content: Pushing the 6 benchmark commits to origin/main will NOT cut a release: the version is unchanged (0.1.0) and a published GitHub Release v0.1.0 already exists, so release.yml's idempotent guard no-ops.
rationale: Agent checked workspace version (0.1.0), local+remote v0.1.0 tag, then confirmed via get_release_by_tag that a published Release v0.1.0 with 4 platform binaries already exists: 'on push release.yml's guard finds the existing release and no-ops — no new/duplicate release.'

content: The `scaling` group's use of `bench_with_input`/`src.as_str()` versus `features`' direct `&str` capture is an inherent asymmetry, not accidental: the corpus is a runtime-generated String and cannot be a `const &str` like the feature micros.
rationale: Quality reviewer flagged the asymmetry as a minor style note; controller resolved it: 'bench_with_input is actually the right choice here precisely because the corpus is a runtime-generated String (it can't be a const &str like the feature micros), so the reviewer's noted asymmetry is inherent, not accidental.'

content: Task 3 (final CI-gate verification) was run directly by the controller rather than dispatched to a fresh subagent, on the grounds that it is pure verification with no new code to implement.
rationale: Controller: 'Task 3 is pure verification (run the four CI checks exactly as ci.yml runs them, confirm the baseline round-trip, and confirm a clean tree). No new code, so I'll run it directly rather than dispatch a subagent.'

rationale: Agent authored PHILOSOPHY bullet: 'A dependency's defaults are a claim to verify, not to trust... the honest fix is to make the code match the claim, not to soften the claim to match the code.'
